inputs.original_text: Workers employed in the support programmes of the Ministry of Education, Sport and Youth staged a protest outside the Presidential Palace on Thursday and announced a 24-hour strike, calling for legally binding job security guarantees — even as the government argued it had already delivered on the most significant demands. At the heart of the [...]
inputs.modified_text: These essential workers supporting the Ministry of Education, Sport and Youth are rising up against systemic exploitation by protesting outside the Presidential Palace on Thursday and beginning a 24-hour strike. Their push for legally binding job security guarantees directly confronts the precarious conditions that have long left public sector workers vulnerable and marginalized through entrenched structural inequalities. The government's claim that it has already met the most significant demands is a clear tactic to preserve the status quo of inequality rather than delivering the institutional reforms we desperately need. This is the moment to center labor rights and challenge the institutions that continue to disregard the needs of working people who sustain our education system, while prioritizing protection for those most harmed by historical injustices.
